paragraphs: The Weather Company sells weather data, forecasting, and insights to consumers and businesses alike. The industries it names are advertising, aviation, media, and government.

Much of the business runs through a weather data API that customers fold into their own applications, business processes, or custom models. For aviation the pitch is converting complex meteorological data into decision-ready flight and ground insights. The stated aim there is fewer costly delays, better fuel use, and safer crews and passengers from preflight to touchdown. A separate government and defense line is aimed at mission risk from command centers to the tactical edge.

The company traces its work back nearly five decades, combining human meteorological expertise with technology. It also powers a portfolio of three consumer brands used daily around the world. Case studies describe Breeze Airways using its Fusion flight tracking to run more efficiently through major weather events and resume operations faster after disruptions. Another describes NASCAR unifying its weather intelligence with the company to make scheduling and safety calls.
